rule_summary: You must be at least 18 to foster. GOV.UK says most fostering services will ask you to be at least 21.
notes: We found no minimum age in the Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011. The Fostering Network says there is no legal lower age limit and 21 is a common service policy.

rule_summary: There is no upper age limit in law. Fostering services can set their own.
notes: UK-wide page. The GOV.UK who-can-foster page gives no upper age limit.

rule_summary: The Regulations approve individuals, not couples. Two people who will share the care of a child should be assessed and approved jointly.
notes: DfE statutory guidance, July 2013. Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, Sch 3 para 10 asks for details of any current or previous marriage, civil partnership or similar relationship.

rule_summary: No income rule was found. The assessment covers past and present employment and standard of living.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, Sch 3 para 14
notes: GOV.UK says you may be able to work and foster, depending on the child and the fostering service.

rule_summary: You do not need to own your home to foster.
notes: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, Sch 3 para 5 asks for particulars of the applicant's accommodation. No tenure rule was found.

rule_summary: Each foster child over 3 should have their own bedroom. Sharing needs each child's responsible authority to agree, and a written assessment.
legal_citation: Fostering Services National Minimum Standards 2011, standard 10.6
notes: GOV.UK says you will usually need a spare bedroom. DfE consulted on replacement standards from 8 July to 16 September 2026; the 2011 standards apply until replaced.

rule_summary: A person may not foster more than three children, the usual fostering limit. Sibling groups and local authority exemptions can go above it.
legal_citation: Children Act 1989, Sch 7 paras 2 to 4
notes: Extends to England and Wales. The limit counts fostered children, not the carer's own. Under para 5, a carer in England who goes over it without exemption is treated as running a children's home.

rule_summary: The applicant and every household member aged 18 or over need an enhanced criminal record certificate that includes children's barred list information.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, Sch 3 para 9
notes: Sch 3 refers to suitability information relating to children under section 113BA of the Police Act 1997. GOV.UK calls this an enhanced with barred lists DBS check.

rule_summary: No one can be approved if they, or an adult in their household, were convicted or cautioned for a specified offence as an adult.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, reg 26(5) to (8)
notes: Specified offences include offences against children and those listed in Sch 4. Reg 26(8) lets a service approve a relative, or the child's current foster parent, if that child's welfare requires it.

rule_summary: The service must interview at least two people the applicant nominates as personal referees, and write a report of each interview.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, reg 26(1A)(c)
notes: If the applicant fostered for another service in the past 12 months, that service is asked for a written reference (reg 26(1A)(b)).

rule_summary: The assessment must include details of the applicant's health, supported by a medical report.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, Sch 3 para 2
notes: GOV.UK says the medical statement usually comes from a GP.

rule_summary: Assessment has two stages. Stage 1 gathers checks, health and references; stage 2 covers personality, background, beliefs and skills, then a report goes to panel.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, reg 26 and Sch 3
notes: Stages can run at the same time. The applicant gets a copy of the report and 10 working days to comment (reg 26(2)(d)).

rule_summary: CoramBAAF publishes Form F (Prospective Foster Carer Report) England as an assessment framework. The 2025 edition replaced the 2018 edition.
notes: Form F is a licensed form: named here, not reproduced. The Regulations require a written report but do not name a format.

rule_summary: Prospective foster carers must be prepared for fostering, with practical techniques for the issues they are likely to meet.
legal_citation: Fostering Services National Minimum Standards 2011, standard 13.3
notes: GOV.UK says the service asks you to go to a preparation course. No set number of hours was found. DfE consulted on replacement standards from 8 July to 16 September 2026; the 2011 standards apply until replaced.

rule_summary: Foster carers must show they have met the Training, Support and Development Standards within 12 months of approval. Family and friends carers have 18 months.
legal_citation: Fostering Services National Minimum Standards 2011, standard 20.3
notes: Standard 20.5 adds a personal development plan for ongoing training. GOV.UK says the TSD workbook is due within 12 months. DfE consulted on replacement standards from 8 July to 16 September 2026; the 2011 standards apply until replaced.

rule_summary: Approval must be reviewed within a year, then at least once a year. The first review must go to the fostering panel.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, reg 28(2) and (5)
notes: We found no fixed end date for approval; it continues subject to review.

rule_summary: The fostering panel should make its recommendation within eight months of receiving the application to be assessed.
legal_citation: Fostering Services National Minimum Standards 2011, standard 14.4
notes: DfE statutory guidance (July 2013) says the same. GOV.UK says the process can take up to 8 months.

rule_summary: A decision that someone is unsuitable after stage 1 must come within 10 working days of having all stage 1 information. Otherwise stage 2 goes ahead.
legal_citation: Fostering Services (England) Regulations 2011, reg 26(1C) and (2)

rule_summary: The 2026 to 2027 national minimum allowance starts at £176 a week, for a child aged 0 to 2 in the rest of England.
legal_citation: Fostering Services National Minimum Standards 2011, standard 28.1
notes: Separate rates for London and the South East. Highest band: £309 a week, age 16 to 17 in London. Updated every April. No minimum allowance once the child turns 18.

rule_summary: We found no minimum age in the Welsh fostering regulations. Foster Wales says being young does not stop you fostering.
notes: Checked the Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018 (SI 2018/1333). Foster Wales is the national network of the 22 local authority fostering services. Some local Foster Wales pages seen in search results give 18 or 21.

rule_summary: There is no upper age limit for fostering, Foster Wales says.
notes: The page says carers can be in their 20s or in their 70s.

rule_summary: Being in a relationship is not required, and marriage or civil partnership is not a condition. Single people and couples can foster.
notes: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, Sch 1 para 10 asks for details of current and previous marriage, civil partnership or similar relationship.

rule_summary: No income rule was found. Foster Wales says not being in work will not stop you becoming a foster carer.
notes: The Foster Wales pay guide says the assessment covers family income and outgoings. Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, Sch 1 para 15 covers employment and standard of living.

rule_summary: You can foster whether you own your home or rent it.
You do not need a large house, but you do need a spare room for the child.
notes: No national standard on bedroom sharing was found in the Welsh regulations read.

rule_summary: A person may not foster more than three children, unless they are all siblings or the local authority grants an exemption.
legal_citation: Children Act 1989, Sch 7 paras 2 to 4
notes: Schedule 7 extends to England and Wales. Foster Wales says carers can usually care for up to three children at once.

rule_summary: The applicant and every household member aged 18 or over need an enhanced criminal record certificate that includes children's barred list information.
legal_citation: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, Sch 1 para 9
notes: Schedule 1 refers to suitability information relating to children under section 113BA of the Police Act 1997. Foster Wales says the process includes a DBS check.

rule_summary: No one can be approved if they, or an adult in their household, were convicted or cautioned for a specified offence as an adult.
legal_citation: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, reg 7(8) to (11)
notes: Reg 7(11) allows approval for a particular child where the person is connected to the child or already fosters them, and the child's welfare requires it.

rule_summary: The service must interview at least two people the applicant nominates as personal referees, and write a report of each interview.
legal_citation: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, reg 7(2)(c)
notes: If the applicant fostered for another service in the past three years, that service is asked for a written reference (reg 7(2)(b)). England's look-back is 12 months.

rule_summary: The assessment must include details of the applicant's health, supported by a medical report.
legal_citation: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, Sch 1 para 2
notes: Foster Wales says the process includes a medical assessment.

rule_summary: The service first gathers Schedule 1 Part 1 checks, then Part 2 information, or Part 3 for relatives and friends. A written report goes to the fostering panel.
legal_citation: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, reg 7 and Sch 1
notes: Part 3 was added from 1 April 2026 by SI 2026/16. Part 2 includes capacity to support a child's sexual orientation and gender identity. The applicant has 10 working days to comment on the report.

rule_summary: CoramBAAF publishes Form F (Prospective Foster Carer Report) Wales, 2026 edition, in English and Welsh. A Form FR for foster carer reviews is also listed.
notes: Form F is a licensed form: named here, not reproduced. The Regulations require a written report but do not name a format.

rule_summary: Local authority fostering services must make sure prospective foster parents get the training, information and advice they consider necessary.
legal_citation: Local Authority Fostering Services (Wales) Regulations 2018, reg 41(3)
notes: Applies to local authority services. Independent services in Wales are covered by separate 2019 regulations, not checked here.

rule_summary: Most local authorities in Wales use The Fostering Network's Skills to Foster course as pre-approval training.
notes: A carer quoted on the page describes a three-day course. No required hours were found.

rule_summary: New carers follow a 'Your First Year' learning programme. Each carer keeps a personal learning plan, reviewed every year with their supervising social worker.
notes: Foster Wales says some courses are required of every carer. Local Authority Fostering Services (Wales) Regulations 2018, reg 41(2) requires necessary training for foster parents. No national deadline for completing set training was found.

rule_summary: Approval must be reviewed within one year, then at least once a year. The first review must go to the fostering panel.
legal_citation: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, reg 9(2) and (5)
notes: Foster Wales says each carer also has a yearly review of learning needs.

rule_summary: A decision that someone is unsuitable after the first checks must come within 10 working days of having all that information. Otherwise the full assessment goes ahead.
legal_citation: Fostering Panels (Establishment and Functions) (Wales) Regulations 2018, reg 7(4)(c) and (5)

rule_summary: Once you apply, approval generally takes about six months, Foster Wales says.
notes: No time limit for the whole assessment was found in the Welsh regulations read. Foster Wales common questions also say around 6 months.

rule_summary: The national minimum allowance for 2026 to 2027 is lowest at £208 a week, for children aged 5 to 15.
notes: Ages 0 to 4: £229; ages 16 to 17: £260. Foster Wales credits the table to The Fostering Network, which reports a 2.2% uplift announced in February 2026. The Welsh Government rate letter for 2026 to 2027 was not found.

rule_summary: You can foster from age 18. Some agencies will not let you foster until you are 21.
notes: We found no minimum age in the Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009.

rule_summary: There is no upper age limit.
You can foster whatever your marital status, sexual orientation or religion. These are protected characteristics under the Equality Act.
notes: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, Sch 3 para 1 asks for marital or civil partnership status. Scottish Government guidance (2010, marked as superseded by 2011 guidance) says the regulations no longer specify which family types can foster.

rule_summary: No income rule was found. The assessment checks your finances.
notes: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, Sch 3 para 7 covers employment and standard of living. mygov.scot says working full-time does not bar you, though some councils limit the types of fostering.

rule_summary: You can foster whether you rent or own your home.
You need a spare bedroom. Some local councils may make exceptions depending on the child's age.
A local authority must not place a child if it would mean more than 3 children placed with one foster carer at a time.
legal_citation: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, reg 27A
notes: Exceptions: a group of more than 3 siblings, emergency or short placements under 4 weeks, and exceptional approval under reg 27B. The limit counts placed children, not the carer's own.

rule_summary: The information for panel must include any criminal convictions, including spent convictions that may lawfully be disclosed.
legal_citation: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, Sch 3 para 10
notes: mygov.scot says the assessment checks your criminal record.

rule_summary: Foster care is a regulated role with children, so membership of the Protecting Vulnerable Groups (PVG) scheme is mandatory.
legal_citation: Disclosure (Scotland) Act 2020, sch 3 (substituted schedule, Part 2 para 4)
notes: From the Act's explanatory notes, para 203; covers kinship placements made by councils too. mygov.scot says PVG membership lasts five years. A start date of 1 April 2025 was seen only in search results.

rule_summary: The information for panel must include references from third parties on the applicant's character and suitability.
legal_citation: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, Sch 3 para 14
notes: No number of referees is set in Schedule 3. mygov.scot says applicants list referees in their application.

rule_summary: The information for panel must include the applicant's health, supported by a medical report.
legal_citation: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, Sch 3 para 1

rule_summary: The local authority refers each case to a fostering panel with the Schedule 3 information, including home, family, beliefs, work, motivation and references.
legal_citation: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, reg 22 and Sch 3
notes: mygov.scot says a social worker visits at home and the assessment checks medical history, criminal record, finances and the home.

rule_summary: CoramBAAF publishes Form F (Scotland), a prospective foster carer report, and a guide for social workers completing it.
notes: Form F is a licensed form: named here, not reproduced. Search results give the Scottish edition as 2016 and mention a pilot of a revised form; not confirmed.

rule_summary: You must attend foster care preparation groups during the application process.
notes: The SSSC Standard for Foster Care (2017) sets learning expectations before approval. No required hours were found.

rule_summary: The SSSC Standard for Foster Care (2017) sets learning stages before approval, after approval and for continuing development. Provision varies by local authority.
notes: From the Scottish Government's Future of Foster Care consultation. It says stakeholders report the Standard has not been fully implemented. No national hours or deadline were found.

rule_summary: Approval must be reviewed within 12 months, then within 3 years of each previous review. Each review goes to the fostering panel.
legal_citation: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, reg 25(1) and (2)
notes: An extra review is needed when a child's welfare requires it (reg 25(8)). mygov.scot says reviews after the first are every 2 years.

rule_summary: The assessment can take 6 to 12 months, mygov.scot says.
notes: Scottish Government guidance (2010, marked as superseded) said authorities should normally aim to finish within six months. No statutory limit was found.

rule_summary: After the panel recommends, the local authority must decide within 14 days and tell the applicant in writing within 7 days of deciding.
legal_citation: Looked After Children (Scotland) Regulations 2009, reg 22(3) and (7)

rule_summary: The Scottish Recommended Allowance for 2026 to 2027 is lowest at £177.68 a week, for children aged 0 to 4.
notes: Ages 5 to 15: £206.71; 16 and over: £283.35. An agreement between the Scottish Government and local authorities, who pay it; independent agencies set their own. Backdated to 1 April 2026 where needed.

rule_summary: You must be 21 or over to foster with HSC NI Foster Care, the Health and Social Care Trusts' fostering service.
notes: This is the service's rule. The Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996 ask for the applicant's age (Sch 1 para 1) but we found no minimum. nidirect gives no minimum age.

rule_summary: There is no maximum age limit for foster or kinship foster carers.
You can apply whether you are single, married or live with a partner.
notes: Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996, Sch 1 para 1 asks for marital status, including any previous marriage.

rule_summary: No income rule was found. You can apply whether you are employed or out of work.
notes: HSC NI says you can apply if employed or claiming benefits. Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996, Sch 1 para 7 covers employment and standard of living.

rule_summary: You can apply whether you live in your own home or rent.
A spare bedroom is ideal but not required. Each foster child must have their own bed and may share a room.
notes: HSC NI says young refugees, and short-break care for disabled children, need a spare bedroom.

rule_summary: A person shall not foster more than three children, unless they are all siblings or the authority grants an exemption.
legal_citation: Children (Northern Ireland) Order 1995, Sch 5 paras 2 to 4
notes: The limit counts fostered children, not the carer's own.

rule_summary: The assessment covers the previous criminal convictions of the applicant and other adults in the household.
legal_citation: Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996, Sch 1 para 9
notes: Subject to the Rehabilitation of Offenders (Northern Ireland) Order 1978. legislation.gov.uk holds these Regulations in their original (as made) form only. Draft replacement regulations (2025) were not found as made on the date checked.

rule_summary: Safeguarding checks include an AccessNI check and a social services check.
notes: HSC NI says foster carers must not have a police record for violent or sexual offences.

rule_summary: Before approval, the applicant must name two personal referees, and the service must arrange for both to be interviewed.
legal_citation: Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996, reg 3(4)(a)
notes: legislation.gov.uk holds these Regulations in their original (as made) form only. Draft replacement regulations (2025) were not found as made on the date checked.

rule_summary: The assessment covers the applicant's health, supported by a medical report.
legal_citation: Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996, Sch 1 para 1
notes: nidirect says applicants are asked for a medical with their GP.

rule_summary: Before approval, the service must get the Schedule 1 information as far as practicable and be satisfied the person and household are suitable.
legal_citation: Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996, reg 3(4)(b) and Sch 1
notes: HSC NI describes a strengths-based assessment by a social worker, with a report to the Foster Care Panel. legislation.gov.uk holds these Regulations in their original (as made) form only. Draft replacement regulations (2025) were not found as made on the date checked.

rule_summary: CoramBAAF lists Form F (Fostering Northern Ireland), 2016 edition, among its Northern Ireland assessment forms.
notes: Form F is a licensed form: named here, not reproduced. Which form each service uses was not checked.

rule_summary: All enquirers are invited to a preparation course, Skills to Foster, before they complete a full application.
notes: HSC NI Adoption and Foster Care recruits and assesses for the five Health and Social Care Trusts. No required hours were found.

rule_summary: All foster and kinship foster carers get ongoing training. HSC NI publishes a learning and development programme for each Trust area.
notes: nidirect also says all carers get training. No required hours or deadline were found.

rule_summary: The approving authority must review approval at intervals of not more than a year.
legal_citation: Foster Placement (Children) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 1996, reg 4(1)
notes: nidirect says all foster and kinship foster carers are reviewed every year. legislation.gov.uk holds these Regulations in their original (as made) form only. Draft replacement regulations (2025) were not found as made on the date checked.

rule_summary: HSC NI says a social worker will call within two days of your contact, then meet you within ten days of that call.
notes: These are first-contact promises, not a limit for the whole assessment. No time limit for the assessment was found in the 1996 Regulations.

rule_summary: The foster care allowance for 2026 to 2027 is lowest at £160 a week, for children aged 0 to 4.
notes: Ages 5 to 10: £179; 11 to 15: £200; 16 to 17: £235. A 3% uplift announced May 2026, backdated. The Department of Health page lists a 2026-27 allowances document, but robots.txt blocks the PDF, so it was not read. nidirect still shows 2024 rates (£149). Paid every 28 days.
